providers.name: BidLens

pricing.plansText: Starter £49/month; Pro £99/month; Team £199/month. Annual billing is available on request, but no annual figures are published.
pricing.seatDetail: No included-user count or additional-seat price is publicly stated. Plans instead limit capability profiles to 1, 3 or 5.
pricing.vatDetail: Prices exclude VAT, which is added at checkout where applicable.
pricing.trialDetail: No free trial. A no-card sample digest is offered; the provider advertises a first-month satisfaction refund and a 14-day cancellation right.

comparablePlans.notes: Monthly subscription; up to 50 alerts per month and a weekly digest. Prices exclude VAT. Annual billing is available on request without a published total.
Monthly subscription; unlimited alerts, CSV export and daily or weekly digest. Prices exclude VAT. Annual billing is available on request without a published total.
Monthly subscription; CSV export, API access and webhook delivery. Prices exclude VAT. Annual billing is available on request without a published total.

comparablePlans.includedUsers: Not publicly stated; offered for more than 5 capability profiles
comparablePlans.notes: Contact the provider for a custom plan; no numeric price is published.

semanticAiMatching.detail: Each release is scored against a capability profile using sector, region, buyer type, value band and semantic fit, with the component scores exposed.

buyerProfiles.detail: No structured buyer-profile or contracting-authority intelligence feature was established on the reviewed pages.

supplierProfiles.detail: Capability profiles describe the subscriber's own business and do not establish supplier, incumbent or competitor profiles.

renewalSignals.detail: No contract-expiry, renewal, re-tender or extension-monitoring feature was established.

similarContracts.detail: No comparable historical contract or award feature was established.

buyerDocuments.detail: No buyer plans, policies, strategies, minutes, budgets or other buyer-document library was established.

buyerRequirements.detail: No extracted participation conditions, certifications, policies or evaluation criteria feature was established.

requirementsPlanning.detail: No readiness, evidence-gap or requirements-planning workflow was established.

awardHistory.detail: The provider says it processes procurement releases, but the reviewed pages do not establish a searchable historical-award feature.

frameworks.detail: No framework, DPS or dynamic-market discovery feature was established.

competitorTracking.detail: No competitor, incumbent, supplier or winner tracking feature was established.

exportsApi.detail: The complete normalized capability is offered on current paid tiers: Pro and Team include CSV export, while Team includes API access and webhook delivery.

collaboration.detail: A Team plan is named, but the reviewed pages do not state included users, shared workspaces, assignments or comments.

bidWriting.detail: No bid drafting, answer library, tender-document analysis or managed writing feature was established.

explicitPortals.detail: The current homepage says BidLens reads every release from Find a Tender.
The current homepage says BidLens reads every release from Contracts Finder.

otherCoverageClaims.claim: The homepage markets UK-wide tender monitoring, but its specific ingestion description names only the Find a Tender and Contracts Finder OCDS feeds.

deepAudit.researchSummary: BidLens sells a lightweight, profile-based tender digest to UK SMEs rather than a broad procurement-intelligence workspace. Its defensible depth is the clearly documented semantic scoring stack and simple OCDS-feed delivery model; it does not publicly establish buyer, supplier, renewal or historical-award intelligence.

legalAndMaturity.detail: The product publishes terms, privacy and refund pages dated May 2026 and describes itself as UK-run, but the terms identify the operator only as 'BidLens' and publish no legal entity, company number or registered address. No exact-name Companies House record was established in this audit, so contracting identity should be confirmed before purchase.

targetCustomerAndUseCase.detail: The site explicitly targets UK SMEs that want a small number of scored matches rather than large spreadsheets. Consultancies can buy multiple capability profiles, with a custom option above five profiles.

dataSourcesAndCoverageMethod.detail: The current homepage and terms both identify official OCDS feeds from Find a Tender and Contracts Finder, say releases are read directly rather than scraped, and describe roughly 150–400 new tenders per day. No other named source is established on the current pages.

dataIngestionAndFreshness.detail: BidLens says it pulls official feeds every day and sees releases when buyers publish, then delivers daily or weekly digests by plan. It publishes no ingestion status page, measured latency, retry policy, upstream outage history or service-level commitment.

matchingAndQualificationMethod.detail: A subscriber provides sectors, regions, value range and free-text capability. BidLens embeds the capability text semantically and combines semantic similarity with sector, region, buyer type and value-band components; the user sets a minimum score and sees the scored summary.

buyerEntityInvestment.detail: No public evidence establishes canonical buyer entities, aliases, deduplication, buyer history or cross-notice buyer profiles.

supplierEntityInvestment.detail: No public evidence establishes supplier or incumbent entities. Subscriber capability profiles are matching inputs, not market-wide supplier profiles.

renewalSignalMethod.detail: No contract-end, extension, expiry-window, re-tender prediction or confirmed-future-notice workflow was established.

requirementsPlanningMethod.detail: No extraction, checklist or durable workflow for requirements, evidence gaps, owners, actions, dates or readiness state was established.

historicalAndAwardDepth.detail: The public product describes scoring new procurement releases but does not document searchable award history, comparable awards or a historical lookback period.

workflowAndIntegrations.detail: Delivery supports email and Telegram on all tiers, CSV export on Pro and Team, and API plus webhooks on Team. The site does not document shared pipelines, assignment, comments or a multi-user permission model.

securitySupportAndOnboarding.detail: The privacy policy states UK-hosted servers, a 90-day post-subscription deletion window, export/deletion rights, Stripe-hosted payments and named AI processors Anthropic and Voyage AI; capability text is sent to Voyage for embedding under commercial no-training terms. Onboarding is a capability profile and delivery preferences, with email support, but no security certification, DPA template, penetration-test statement, uptime history or formal support SLA is published.

commercialModel.detail: Public month-to-month prices are £49, £99 and £199 excluding VAT, differentiated mainly by capability profiles, cadence, alert volume and export/integration rights. Annual billing is manually available but no numeric annual price is published; no free trial is offered, although a sample digest and first-month satisfaction refund are described.

materialLimitations.detail: Coverage is limited to two named national feeds; devolved portals, private portal tender packs and historical intelligence are not publicly established.
The Team label does not establish seats or collaboration; it buys more profiles and technical delivery options.

diligenceQuestions: What is the contracting legal entity, company number and registered address behind BidLens?
What measured source-to-alert latency, retry process and outage notification applies when an OCDS feed fails?
How many users can access each plan, and are API rate limits, webhook retries and schemas documented?
Can the provider supply a DPA, subprocessor list, security controls and deletion evidence for capability-profile data?

caveats: The current homepage and terms establish only Find a Tender and Contracts Finder; broader UK-wide marketing should not be read as evidence of devolved-portal coverage.
The scoring, coverage and delivery claims are provider-stated and were not independently tested by Civensa.
Seat entitlement is not publicly stated even though a Team plan is offered.
The contracting legal entity and company number are not stated on the reviewed legal pages.

providers.name: BidScout

pricing.plansText: Starter, Professional and Enterprise tiers are published, but no numeric paid subscription price is displayed. Professional includes full tender intelligence, AI bid writing, Bid/No-Bid scoring and Market Intelligence; Enterprise adds consortium tools, advanced analytics, support and custom integrations.
pricing.seatDetail: Included users and additional-seat pricing are not publicly stated.
pricing.vatDetail: VAT treatment is not publicly stated.
pricing.trialDetail: The pricing page advertises a 7-day Starter trial without a credit card. Another first-party comparison page references a 14-day trial, so confirm the current trial at signup.

comparablePlans.notes: A 7-day no-card trial is advertised; no post-trial numeric price or billing period is published.
Paid tier described publicly, but numeric price and billing period are not published.
Custom integrations and support are described; contact the provider for a quote.

semanticAiMatching.detail: BidScout documents AI Bid/No-Bid scoring for technical fit, competitive position, resources and relationship, but its alert-matching page describes keyword, CPV and buyer rules rather than semantic alert matching.

buyerProfiles.detail: The Professional-tier Market Intelligence hub includes buyer spend analysis across 8,200+ authorities, but a separate public buyer-profile directory was not established.

supplierProfiles.detail: Public supplier pages aggregate award counts, values, buyers and related opportunities, but the reviewed first-party pages do not establish canonicalisation, deduplication or entity-resolution controls.

renewalSignals.detail: The Contract Renewal Tracker monitors awarded-contract end dates, bands urgency and advertises alerts 90–180 days before expiry with a direct rebid link when published.

similarContracts.detail: Competitor Watch sends similar live opportunities based on a supplier's win history; no notice-level comparable historical-award view was established.

buyerDocuments.detail: The Document Library covers the subscriber's own evidence, policies and case studies; it does not establish a library of buyer plans, strategies, minutes, budgets or other buyer-authored documents beyond notices.

buyerRequirements.detail: Evaluation Criteria Analysis auto-extracts scoring criteria, weightings and mandatory compliance requirements from a tender.

requirementsPlanning.detail: Bid/No-Bid scoring assesses technical fit, resources and relationships, while evaluation analysis highlights mandatory requirements; no explicit gap-remediation or pre-tender evidence-planning workflow was established.

awardHistory.detail: Supplier pages expose historical contract awards, award counts, total values and buyers; alerts can also be configured for new awards.

frameworks.detail: Market Intelligence includes framework analysis, and the provider positions its coverage as including major framework agreements.

competitorTracking.detail: Competitor Watch can monitor a named supplier, email when it wins new contracts and surface similar live opportunities; Market Intelligence includes competitor award tracking and league tables.

exportsApi.detail: The complete normalized capability is offered: BidScout documents Slack, Teams, Salesforce, HubSpot, SharePoint and Google Drive integrations plus bid-document export; Enterprise adds custom integrations. No public API specification was found.

collaboration.detail: A current team workflow is established through shared saved searches, and Enterprise adds consortium tools. Included-user counts and detailed assignment/comment permissions are not public, but plan gating does not downgrade the capability.

bidWriting.detail: Professional includes a complete AI bid-writing workflow backed by the subscriber's document evidence library; Starter exclusion is plan gating, not an incomplete capability.

explicitPortals.detail: Named in the provider's Tender Search coverage and homepage service description.
Named in the provider's Tender Search coverage and homepage service description.
Named as TED/TED Europa in the provider's UK and EU coverage; OJEU records are also referenced.
Explicitly named in the provider's homepage coverage description.

Crown Commercial Service is explicitly named as a covered UK source in the homepage service description.

otherCoverageClaims.claim: The provider states coverage of 50+ official UK and EU procurement portals, 28,800+ live tenders, 8,200+ contracting authorities and 64 countries.
The provider broadly references additional official portals and country portals in France, Germany, Norway, Spain, Italy and elsewhere without naming individual portal products.

deepAudit.researchSummary: BidScout presents a broad UK/EU tender-intelligence and AI bid-writing suite spanning search, alerts, renewals, market analytics, competitor monitoring, drafting and CRM delivery. Its apparent breadth is materially greater than its public diligence depth: implementation detail, numeric pricing, security terms and legal-policy content are thin or absent.

legalAndMaturity.detail: Companies House records an active private company, BIDSCOUT LTD (13530098), incorporated in July 2021 and renamed from Abroad Aspirations Limited on 5 May 2026. The site links privacy and terms URLs, but the reviewed pages expose only the common navigation shell and no substantive policy text, leaving contracting and data-processing terms unclear.

targetCustomerAndUseCase.detail: The product targets bid teams pursuing UK and EU public-sector opportunities, from Starter search and alerts through Professional writing/intelligence and Enterprise consortium, analytics, support and custom integrations.

dataSourcesAndCoverageMethod.detail: BidScout names Find a Tender, Contracts Finder, TED, Public Contracts Scotland, eTendersNI, Sell2Wales and Crown Commercial Service, while marketing 50+ official UK/EU portals, 8,200+ authorities and 64 countries. It does not publish a source inventory for the remaining portals, ingestion method by source, licensing map or reconciliation method for cross-posted notices.

dataIngestionAndFreshness.detail: Smart Alerts promises real-time delivery when notices are published, with instant or daily digests, and the site shows a large live-opportunity count. No per-source poll cadence, observed latency, backfill policy, status page, missed-notice reconciliation or uptime commitment is documented.

matchingAndQualificationMethod.detail: Alert rules use keyword, sector, region, CPV and buyer. Separate AI Bid/No-Bid scoring grades Technical Fit, Competitive Position, Resource Availability and Relationship Score out of 100 and returns a recommendation; this is qualification after discovery rather than documented semantic alert matching.

buyerEntityInvestment.detail: Market Intelligence advertises spend analysis across 8,200+ authorities, which establishes structured cross-notice buyer analytics. The reviewed pages do not explain buyer-name canonicalisation, aliases, organizational hierarchies, deduplication or entity-resolution quality controls.

supplierEntityInvestment.detail: Public supplier pages aggregate awards, buyers, value and related opportunities, but the public directory also exposes raw or ambiguous records such as 'multiple suppliers' and 'not applicable', and near-duplicate supplier-name pages are visible. No alias merge, company-number linkage or deduplication method is documented.

renewalSignalMethod.detail: The Renewal Tracker explicitly monitors awarded-contract end dates, tracks 10,800+ contracts and sends alerts 90–180 days before contract end. It distinguishes the expiry lead from a direct rebid link when a new opportunity is published, but does not explain extension-option handling, uncertain dates or how expected re-tenders are separated from confirmed notices.

requirementsPlanningMethod.detail: Evaluation Criteria Analysis extracts weightings and mandatory requirements, Bid/No-Bid scores resource and relationship fit, and the clarifications feature surfaces documentation gaps and scoring risks. No durable workflow is documented for assigning each gap to an owner, attaching required evidence, setting remediation dates and maintaining readiness before submission.

historicalAndAwardDepth.detail: Supplier pages and Market Intelligence expose award history, buyers, values, competitor league tables and award alerts. The public pages do not state the full historical lookback, award-source completeness, correction policy or whether framework call-offs and duplicate awards are normalized.

workflowAndIntegrations.detail: The integration page documents Slack and Teams alerts, Salesforce and HubSpot pipeline sync, SharePoint and Google Drive document-library connections, plus Zendesk, Copilot and Unleash. Shared saved searches and Enterprise consortium tools establish team use, but included seats, assignment rights, API specifications and integration directionality are not public.

securitySupportAndOnboarding.detail: A seven-day no-card trial, self-guided tour and help page for setup, alerts, writing and billing are public. However, the reviewed privacy and terms URLs contain no substantive policy text, and no encryption, residency, retention, subprocessor, certification, incident-response, status-page, support-hours or SLA detail was established.

commercialModel.detail: Starter, Professional and Enterprise packaging is public, with a trial on Starter and custom integrations/support on Enterprise, but no paid numeric price, currency, VAT treatment, billing period or included-user allowance is disclosed. The page's 'transparent pricing' description therefore cannot be used for normalized cost comparison.

materialLimitations.detail: The security and legal diligence surface is materially incomplete because current privacy and terms URLs do not publish substantive terms.
Coverage, authority counts, renewal inventory and real-time timing are provider claims without a complete source list or published measurement method.

contradictions.detail: The pricing page advertises a seven-day trial, while another first-party comparison page advertises fourteen days.
The about page headline says 12 official sources while body copy claims 50+ official portals; the site does not publish a reconciliation or complete source list.
The pricing page describes its offer as transparent but omits every numeric paid price and billing unit.

diligenceQuestions: Can BidScout provide executed service terms, privacy policy, DPA, subprocessor list, hosting regions, retention schedule and security certifications?
What are the numeric prices, billing basis, VAT treatment, included users and additional-seat costs for each current plan?
Which exact 50+ portals are ingested, by what method and cadence, and how are duplicate notices, buyers and suppliers entity-resolved?
How are renewal dates derived when awards contain durations or extension options, and how are predictions separated from confirmed re-tenders?
Are Salesforce and HubSpot integrations bidirectional, and is there a documented API with authentication, limits and support commitments?

caveats: No numeric paid pricing, seat entitlement, currency or VAT treatment is shown on the checked pricing page despite its 'transparent pricing' description.
First-party pages conflict on trial length: the pricing page says 7 days, while another marketing page says 14 days.
Only explicitly named portals are normalized above; the broader claim of 50+ sources was not expanded into unnamed portals.
Feature, coverage, volume, scoring and renewal claims are provider-stated and were not independently tested by Civensa.

providers.name: BidSkim

pricing.plansText: Free £0 forever. Monitor £79/month or £780/year (£65/month effective). Predict £189/month or £1,860/year (£155/month effective).
pricing.seatDetail: Monitor and Predict can send alerts to the subscriber and up to three teammates. No additional-seat price is published, and the provider directs large bid teams needing seats toward enterprise platforms.
pricing.vatDetail: BidSkim Limited states that it is not VAT registered, so no VAT is charged and displayed prices are final.
pricing.trialDetail: The Free plan requires no card and includes browsing, a one-off match scan and a 12-month report. No paid-plan trial is stated; annual plans have a 30-day money-back guarantee.

comparablePlans.includedUsers: One account per person or business; no paid team seats stated
comparablePlans.notes: Free forever with no card; one match scan and a 12-month report. This is not an annual billing plan.

comparablePlans.includedUsers: Subscriber plus up to 3 additional alert recipients
comparablePlans.notes: Monthly and annual billing are published. No VAT is charged. Annual plans have a 30-day money-back guarantee.

comparablePlans.includedUsers: Subscriber plus up to 3 additional alert recipients
comparablePlans.notes: Monthly and annual billing are published. No VAT is charged. Annual plans have a 30-day money-back guarantee.

semanticAiMatching.detail: Monitor and Predict provide complete ongoing profile-based matching: every new notice is scored 0–100 against services, region, value and certifications with written reasons. The Free plan's one-off scan is plan gating, not an incomplete paid capability.

buyerProfiles.detail: Predict includes structured cross-notice buyer profiles with requirements, spend and award history, top suppliers, contacts, renewals and researched notes. Public data documentation states that repeated notices are deduplicated and lifecycle notices are connected; Predict gating does not downgrade the capability.

supplierProfiles.detail: Predict includes structured supplier and incumbent profiles that aggregate wins, buyers, regions, categories, awarded values, held contracts and renewal exposure across the award record. This is a complete current-plan capability even though public pages do not describe the exact alias-resolution algorithm.

renewalSignals.detail: Predict provides complete renewal timing signals built from public award, contract, modification and termination records. Exact dates, durations and extension options are converted into source-linked planning dates, refreshed daily and ranked against the subscriber profile; the provider explicitly distinguishes these from confirmed re-tender dates.

similarContracts.detail: Predict surfaces comparable historical awards matched by contract scope rather than shared keywords, including winners, values, terms, bid counts and SME status where published. Higher-tier gating does not make the implemented capability partial.

buyerDocuments.detail: The reviewed public pages do not establish a full searchable corpus of buyer-authored documents designed to surface upcoming work.

buyerRequirements.detail: Predict buyer profiles organize insurance, certifications, social-value rules, local preferences and pass/fail gates drawn from public buyer records and documents. The capability is complete on Predict; Monitor exclusion is plan gating.

requirementsPlanning.detail: Predict is positioned for preparing certifications, evidence and answers before a tender goes live using buyer requirements and likely renewals; no separate task-based readiness workflow is described.

awardHistory.detail: The service offers a one-off 12-month matched-award report on Free and five years of connected buyer and award history, comparable awards and supplier intelligence on Predict. Tier-specific lookback and access do not make the capability partial.

frameworks.detail: BidSkim badges frameworks, DPS and dynamic markets, filters out non-joinable call-offs and modifications, and shows application/end dates, supplier caps and route-in information.

competitorTracking.detail: Predict provides complete named-supplier tracking across public-sector wins, buyers, awarded values, regions, categories and contracts nearing expiry. Monitor exclusion is plan gating, not an incomplete implementation.

exportsApi.detail: No CSV/Excel export, API, webhook or CRM integration is documented on the reviewed pages; the pricing page says large teams needing exports may be better served by enterprise platforms.

collaboration.detail: Monitor and Predict can deliver alerts to up to three teammates and include a pipeline, but no multi-user seats, assignments, comments or shared-workspace permissions are documented.

bidWriting.detail: The pricing FAQ explicitly says BidSkim does not write bids and focuses on finding, qualifying and researching opportunities before the bid.

explicitPortals.detail: BidSkim states that it scans this official source in full and links to the official source page.
BidSkim states that it scans this official source in full and links to the official source page.
BidSkim states that it scans this official source in full and links to the official source page.
BidSkim states that it scans this official source in full and links to the official source page.

otherCoverageClaims.claim: The provider states 800,000+ notices, 10,000+ buyers, five years of award history and daily checks across four official British sources.

deepAudit.researchSummary: BidSkim sells SME-focused opportunity qualification and pre-tender intelligence rather than bid-writing software: daily semantic matches on Monitor, with buyer, supplier, award and renewal research on Predict. Its defensible depth is the connected five-year procurement history, evidence-linked contract timing method and explainable capability matching, balanced against narrow four-source coverage and a young operating company.

legalAndMaturity.detail: Companies House records active private company BIDSKIM LTD (17160570), incorporated 15 April 2026 for software development. The website publishes dated terms and privacy policies and identifies the service as operated by 'BidSkim Limited'; buyers should align the exact registered name and contracting documentation.

targetCustomerAndUseCase.detail: The product explicitly targets SMEs, owners and small commercial teams that cannot monitor portals daily. Monitor is for live opportunity prioritisation; Predict is for teams researching buyers, tracking incumbents and preparing months before likely procurements.

dataSourcesAndCoverageMethod.detail: BidSkim names and links four official sources: Find a Tender, Contracts Finder, Public Contracts Scotland and Sell2Wales. Its public method says cross-posted and repeated notices are matched on reference numbers, buyer and dates, collapsed, normalized into common fields, and planning/tender/award/change notices are connected around the same buyer need.

dataIngestionAndFreshness.detail: The four sources are checked daily, new notices are scored for the next morning's feed, and renewal timing candidates are refreshed daily. Every brief retains the official-source link; the terms disclaim completeness and uptime because the service depends on procurement portals and other infrastructure providers.

matchingAndQualificationMethod.detail: BidSkim reads the full notice and scores it 0–100 against services, delivery regions, contract-size range, certifications and route-to-market context. Written reasons are shown, users choose a score threshold, save/dismiss feedback informs matching, and official notices remain linked for verification.

buyerEntityInvestment.detail: Predict provides structured buyer profiles across requirements, contacts, awards, spend patterns, repeat suppliers and renewals, built on a stated 10,000+ buyer corpus and connected lifecycle records. Public evidence establishes notice deduplication and cross-notice aggregation but does not disclose the buyer alias, hierarchy or entity-resolution algorithm, so implementation quality should be tested during diligence.

supplierEntityInvestment.detail: Predict aggregates named suppliers and incumbents across wins, buyers, categories, regions, awarded value and renewal exposure, enabling tracking across the public award record. No publishable detail was found for Companies House linkage, aliases, trading-name merges or duplicate-supplier adjudication.

renewalSignalMethod.detail: The documented method uses public award, contract, modification and termination records. Exact start/end dates, duration, extensions and other dated lifecycle evidence create source-linked planning signals across a 24-month horizon, refreshed daily; missing timing stays missing and the UI treats a signal as a possible buying cycle, not confirmation of re-tender.

requirementsPlanningMethod.detail: Predict combines likely renewals with buyer requirements, contacts, incumbents and comparable awards so teams can prepare certifications, social-value evidence and pass/fail answers early. This is an evidence-backed preparation use case, but no durable in-product gaps/actions/owners/deadlines/readiness workflow is publicly documented.

historicalAndAwardDepth.detail: The product claims 800,000+ notices and five years of connected award history. Predict surfaces scope-matched comparable awards with winners, values, terms, bid counts and SME status where published; Free includes a profile-matched 12-month retrospective award report.

workflowAndIntegrations.detail: Monitor and Predict include a four-stage Saved/Bidding/Submitted/Won pipeline, win-rate view, filters, rescans and alert delivery to the subscriber plus three recipients. The product intentionally does not publish exports, API, CRM integration, true team seats, assignments or comments, and describes enterprise teams as out of scope.

securitySupportAndOnboarding.detail: The privacy policy documents bcrypt password hashing, HTTPS, secure cookies, automatic database backups, 30-day account-deletion completion, EU-region PostHog retention, named processors and consent-controlled analytics; payments use Stripe and hosting uses Render. Setup is advertised at roughly two minutes with no card or sales call, but no security certification, penetration-test report, DPA, public status page or formal support SLA is published.

commercialModel.detail: The model is self-serve per organization: permanent Free, Monitor at £79 monthly or £780 annually, and Predict at £189 monthly or £1,860 annually, with no VAT charged. Annual plans have a 30-day guarantee; users manage plan and billing in Settings, and the product explicitly avoids enterprise seat/export/account-management packaging.

materialLimitations.detail: Named coverage is Britain-only across four sources and excludes eTendersNI; the phrase 'every public notice in Britain' should be interpreted within that declared source scope.
Renewal dates, contacts, requirements, incumbents, bid counts and similar-award fields depend on public-record completeness; the provider says sparse source data is not guessed.
The product does not write bids and is not positioned for large bid teams needing seats, exports, account management or enterprise integrations.

contradictions.detail: The website uses 'BidSkim Limited' for the operator, while the authoritative Companies House record gives the registered name as 'BIDSKIM LTD'; contracting documents should use the exact registered name.

diligenceQuestions: What buyer and supplier alias-resolution rules, corporate identifiers and manual QA are used, and what sampled precision/recall can be shared?
What proportion of renewal signals is based on explicit end dates versus calculated durations or extension evidence, and how is uncertainty presented in exports or UI?
Can the provider supply a DPA, full subprocessor and hosting-region map, recovery objectives, security-test evidence and incident notification terms?
What source-monitoring controls detect a missed daily ingest or cross-source duplicate, and what remediation or customer notice follows?
Are additional alert recipients view-only email recipients, and what roadmap exists for true multi-user permissions or exports?

caveats: Civensa is operated by BidSkim Limited, so this listing requires a prominent ownership disclosure and the same evidence standard used for competitors.
The provider's stated British coverage names four portals and does not include eTendersNI.
Renewal dates, buyer requirements, contacts, bid counts and other enriched fields depend on what public sources publish; the provider says sparse source data is left sparse rather than guessed.
The matching, history, coverage and intelligence claims are provider-stated and were not independently tested by Civensa.

providers.name: BidStats

pricing.plansText: Free £0. Standard £35/month per user or £350/year per user. Pro £80/month for the first three seats or £800/year for the first three seats. Insights starts from £5,000/year.
pricing.seatDetail: Standard is priced per user. Pro includes the first three seats. Extra users are £150 plus VAT each, but the public text does not state the charge period. Included users for Free and Insights are not publicly stated.
pricing.vatDetail: Extra users are explicitly priced at £150 plus VAT; the VAT treatment of base plan prices is not stated on the checked page.
pricing.trialDetail: No trial or payment-card requirement is publicly stated on the checked pricing page.

comparablePlans.notes: Free plan with five tender views per day and 90 days of history; this is not an annual billing plan.

comparablePlans.includedUsers: One user at the published per-user price
comparablePlans.notes: The page's pricing script labels Standard as per user per month or year. Base-plan VAT treatment is not stated.
The page labels the monthly and annual prices as covering the first three seats. Extra users are £150 plus VAT each, with the charge period not stated.
Starting price ('from £5,000 per annum'); actual quote may be higher. Extra-user statement explicitly excludes Insights.

semanticAiMatching.detail: No semantic, machine-learning or profile-based relevance matching feature was established on the reviewed pages.

buyerProfiles.detail: BidStats publishes cross-notice buyer reports with notices, awards, sectors, suppliers and name-grouping sections. Example reports explicitly list names included and excluded, but can group several distinct departments, so robust canonical buyer identity is not established.

supplierProfiles.detail: BidStats publishes cross-notice supplier reports with awards, sectors, values, buyers and explicit included/excluded name groups. Example reports group multiple distinct suppliers under a search concept, so robust canonical supplier identity is not established.

renewalSignals.detail: A complete expiring-contract pipeline is included in Standard, Pro and Insights, using two, five or ten years of awarded-contract coverage respectively. Free-plan exclusion and tiered lookback are plan gating, not an incomplete capability.

similarContracts.detail: Search and analysis pages expose historical notices, but no feature that deliberately surfaces comparable historical contracts against a notice or profile was established.

buyerDocuments.detail: A Knowledge Hub is named on paid plans, but the reviewed pages do not establish that it contains buyer plans, strategies, minutes, budgets or other buyer-authored documents beyond procurement notices.

buyerRequirements.detail: No normalized extraction of certifications, participation conditions, policies or evaluation criteria was established.

requirementsPlanning.detail: No readiness, requirements-gap or evidence-planning workflow was established.

awardHistory.detail: Paid plans provide complete award-history access with awardees and values across two, five or ten years depending on tier, while public supplier and tender pages also expose award records. Tiered history depth does not make the capability partial.

frameworks.detail: Insights includes frameworks data as a complete current-plan capability. Its higher-tier restriction is plan gating, not a partial implementation.

competitorTracking.detail: Supplier reports provide competitor research, but no named-supplier monitoring or competitor alert feature was established.

exportsApi.detail: Pro includes tender and contract export, and Insights includes exports plus CRM connectivity through an API. These complete higher-tier capabilities qualify as yes despite Free and Standard exclusions.

collaboration.detail: Pro includes three seats and extra users can be purchased, establishing current multi-user access. Assignments, shared pipelines, comments and permission detail were not established, but the normalized collaboration definition is met by multiple users.

bidWriting.detail: No bid drafting, response library, document analysis, compliance matrix or managed writing service was established.

explicitPortals.detail: The public site names TED/OJEU as a source for its UK tender search.
The public site names Contracts Finder as a source for its UK tender search.
The public site names Find a Tender as a source for its UK tender search.

otherCoverageClaims.claim: Pro and Insights are described as sourced from more than 3,000 buyers; the application homepage separately says more than 3,600 buyers.

deepAudit.researchSummary: BidStats is a mature tender-search and market-analysis service operated by Oxygen Finance, with free search and paid layers for alerts, awards, expiring contracts, exports, frameworks and API-enabled pre-procurement intelligence. Its strongest defensible depth is long historical coverage and an established corporate operator; its weakest area is entity quality, where public buyer and supplier reports visibly group names without proving robust organizational resolution.

legalAndMaturity.detail: BidStats terms identify Oxygen Finance Limited as supplier. Companies House records Oxygen Finance Limited (05288899) as active, incorporated in November 2004, with medium-company accounts through 2025; this is materially more established than newly formed specialist competitors.

targetCustomerAndUseCase.detail: The service spans occasional free search, Standard users needing daily alerts and expiry pipeline, three-seat Pro teams needing deeper history and exports, and Insights customers needing frameworks, pre-procurement leads, decision-maker contacts and CRM API connectivity. The pricing page states 80,000+ users.

dataSourcesAndCoverageMethod.detail: Public search explicitly names Find a Tender, Contracts Finder and TED/OJEU, while pricing and homepage copy claim sourcing from 3,000+ or 3,600+ buyers. Public terms acknowledge reliance on third-party portals and official publications, but no full buyer/source inventory, portal-by-portal ingestion method or coverage reconciliation is published.

dataIngestionAndFreshness.detail: The homepage says data is sourced daily and paid alerts are delivered daily. No public status page, per-source latency, retry/backfill policy, missed-notice reconciliation metric or uptime SLA was found; the terms disclaim third-party portal availability and data accuracy/completeness.

matchingAndQualificationMethod.detail: BidStats supports keyword searches, daily tender and award notifiers, source/region/value/buyer-type/sector filters and CPV-derived keyword analysis. No semantic, profile-based or AI relevance-scoring method was established on the reviewed public pages.

buyerEntityInvestment.detail: Buyer reports aggregate notices, awards, suppliers, sectors and geography and explicitly expose names included and excluded from a report. Sampled broad reports can merge distinct departments under one concept, so the public evidence shows grouping investment but not reliable canonical buyer entities, hierarchy or alias adjudication.

supplierEntityInvestment.detail: Supplier reports aggregate awards, values, buyers, sectors and geography and expose included/excluded name groups. The sampled 'Insight' report groups multiple distinct organizations under a search concept, so company-number linkage, aliases, trading-name merges and canonical supplier identity are not established.

renewalSignalMethod.detail: Standard, Pro and Insights include an 'Expiring contracts pipeline' built from contracts awarded in the prior two, five or ten years, and legacy first-party copy says the technology predicts tenders before publication. Public documentation does not distinguish explicit contract-end dates, calculated durations, extension options, predicted windows and confirmed future notices.

requirementsPlanningMethod.detail: No extraction of buyer requirements and no durable readiness workflow for gaps, evidence, owners, actions, deadlines or readiness state was established. A Knowledge Hub label alone does not establish its content or planning method.

historicalAndAwardDepth.detail: History scales from 90 days on Free to two years on Standard, five years on Pro and ten years on Insights. Paid plans expose awardees and values and power expiring-contract pipelines over the same lookback, while public tender, buyer and supplier pages make substantial award records discoverable.

workflowAndIntegrations.detail: The product documents bookmarked tenders and folders, daily notifiers, Pro export with three seats, and Insights CRM connectivity via API. It does not publish the API specification, supported CRMs, sync direction, assignments, comments, shared pipeline behavior or role permissions.

securitySupportAndOnboarding.detail: Oxygen publishes a privacy policy, ICO registration, data-processing policy and BidStats terms with confidentiality obligations; its privacy policy describes access controls, breach procedures and international-transfer safeguards. Retention details are available on request rather than product-specific public schedules, and no BidStats security certification, penetration-test statement, public status page or support SLA was found. Terms also permit use of customer feedback/content to improve products, including training AI/ML technologies, which enterprise buyers should scope precisely.

commercialModel.detail: Free, Standard, Pro and custom Insights tiers are publicly packaged. Standard is £35 monthly per user or £350 annually; Pro is £80 monthly or £800 annually for three seats; Insights starts at £5,000 annually. Extra users cost £150 plus VAT, but the charge period is not stated, and VAT treatment for base plans is not explicit.

materialLimitations.detail: Buyer and supplier reports provide useful aggregation but sampled broad names can merge distinct organizations, limiting canonical entity confidence.
Renewal methodology is not public enough to separate exact published expiry dates from modelled or calculated future-tender predictions.
Source coverage, history, alert capacity, exports, frameworks, API and seats vary materially by plan.

contradictions.detail: The current application homepage uses both '3,000+ buyers' and 'over 3,600 buyers' on the same page, while pricing uses 3,000+ for Pro and Insights.

diligenceQuestions: Which exact portals and buyer organizations make up the advertised coverage, and why do current pages state both 3,000+ and 3,600+ buyers?
How are buyer and supplier aliases resolved, and can records be anchored to organization or Companies House identifiers rather than broad name groups?
How does the expiring-contract pipeline distinguish published end dates, duration-derived dates, extension options, predicted re-tender timing and confirmed notices?
Which customer content can be used for AI/ML training under clause 14.3, and can enterprise customers opt out contractually?
What CRM systems and API operations are supported, and what are the API limits, security model, support hours and service levels?
Is the £150 plus VAT extra-user charge monthly, annual or one-time, and are base subscription prices VAT-inclusive?

caveats: Source count, history depth, alert capacity, exports, frameworks and renewal coverage differ materially by plan.

Buyer and supplier reports expose included and excluded name groups, but sampled reports can cluster distinct organisations; Civensa therefore records both profile capabilities as partial rather than canonical entity profiles.
The site currently uses both 3,000+ and 3,600+ buyer-count claims on first-party pages; neither was independently verified by Civensa.
The explicitly named source list on the public search page is narrower than the 3,000+ buyer coverage claim and does not name devolved portals individually.
Pricing, data coverage and feature claims are provider-stated and were not independently tested by Civensa.
